errata.notes: Each of the three tables in Appendix A contain two entries for state 0, the first of which in each case incorrectly reports the Number_Of_Bits as 0. The all-zero rows should be removed.

The offset_value in the second-to-last line in the table should be 3, not 1. This line intends to demonstrate the property described earlier in the section that when the sequence's literals_length is 0, an offset_value of 3 resolves to Repeated_Offset1 - 1 and is inserted at the head of the Repeated_Offsets. This is the behavior that is reflected in the rest of the row, which an offset_value of 1 would not trigger (the resolved offset would be 2222, not 2221, and the Repeated_Offsets would remain unchanged, as demonstrated in the 3rd row of the table).

(I wrote this table and it read 3 in the version I provided to the document authors--a typo was introduced somewhere.)

errata.correct:
Size_Format == 01:  4 streams.  Both Regenerated_Size and
   Compressed_Size use 10 bits (values 6-1023).
   Literals_Section_Header uses 3 bytes.

Size_Format == 10:  4 streams.  Both Regenerated_Size and
   Compressed_Size use 14 bits (values 6-16383).
   Literals_Section_Header uses 4 bytes.

Size_Format == 11:  4 streams.  Both Regenerated_Size and
   Compressed_Size use 18 bits (values 6-262143).
   Literals_Section_Header uses 5 bytes.
errata.notes:
The calculation for the size of the fourth stream, specified in section 3.1.1.3.1.6, will underflow if the total size of the literals in the block is less than 6 bytes. So the 4-stream mode cannot be used in blocks with fewer than 6 literals. (Nor should it be, since it is strictly less efficient for very small literal sections.)

The source for this errata is https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/3398.

[Verifier note: Confirmed with zstd developers.]

Section 3.1.1.3.1 describes the Literals_Section mentioned in and linked from Section 3.1.1.3 Compressed Blocks. However, the section is labeled as Literals_Section_Header resulting in two sections both labeled Literals_Section_Header (sections 3.1.1.3.1 and 3.1.1.3.1.1).

According to the description in 3.1.1.5, an offset value 1 with literal length 0 shall use Repeated Offset 2. However, in the last row of the example table, this is not the case. Since the second-to-last row has no "3333" value, I believe that the fifth column in the last row should be "1111".

errata.orig:
[...] For Treeless_Literals_Block, the Huffman table comes from
the previously compressed literals block, or from a dictionary; [...]
errata.correct:
[...] For Treeless_Literals_Block, the Huffman table comes from
the previous Compressed_Literals_Block, or from a dictionary; [...]
errata.notes:
The corrected text follows the description of Treeless_Literals_Block in section "3.1.1.3.1.1. Literals_Section_Header":

"Treeless_Literals_Block:
    This is a Huffman-compressed block, using the Huffman tree from the previous
    Compressed_Literals_Block or a dictionary if there is no previous Huffman-compressed
    literals block. [...]"

At the very least, the "previously" in the original text should be replaced by "previous".

errata.orig:
Within private environments, any dictionary ID can be used.  However,
   for frames and dictionaries distributed in public space,
   Dictionary_ID must be attributed carefully.  The following ranges are
   reserved for use only with dictionaries that have been registered
   with IANA (see Section 7.4):

   low range:  <= 32767

   high range:  >= (1 << 31)

   Any other value for Dictionary_ID can be used by private arrangement
   between participants.

   Any payload presented for decompression that references an
   unregistered reserved dictionary ID results in an error.
errata.correct:
Within private environments, any dictionary ID can be used.  However,
   for frames and dictionaries distributed in public space,
   Dictionary_ID must be attributed carefully.  The following ranges are
   reserved for use only with dictionaries that have been registered
   with IANA (see Section 7.4):

   low range:  <= 32767

   high range:  >= (1 << 31)

   Any other value for Dictionary_ID can be used by private arrangement
   between participants.

   Any payload presented for decompression that references a dictionary
   ID for which the referenced dictionary is not available to the decoder
   results in an error.
errata.notes:
The phrase "unregistered reserved dictionary ID" is not implementable
(a decoder cannot determine IANA registration status) and conflicts with
the earlier sentence permitting any ID in private environments.
Section 5 uses conditional phrasing ("If ... distributed in a private
environment"), and Section 7.4 states that at publication no IANA
registry existed.  The correction makes the error condition decoder-side
(dictionary not available locally) rather than registry-side.

errata.orig:
A compliant decompressor must be able to decompress at least one
   working set of parameters that conforms to the specifications
   presented here.  It may also ignore informative fields, such as the
   checksum.  Whenever it does not support a parameter defined in the
   compressed stream, it must produce an unambiguous error code and
   associated error message explaining which parameter is unsupported.
errata.correct:
A compliant decompressor must be able to decompress at least one
   working set of parameters that conforms to the specifications
   presented here.  Whenever it does not support a parameter defined in
   the compressed stream, it must produce an unambiguous error code and
   associated error message explaining which parameter is unsupported.
   The Content_Checksum (Section 3.1.1.1.1.5), when present, SHOULD be
   verified; a mismatch indicates data corruption.
errata.notes:
The term "informative fields" is not defined anywhere in this document
(the phrase occurs once), and its only example is the Content_Checksum
-- the only mechanism the format provides for detecting corruption of
the decoded data.  No other part of the document requires a decoder to
verify it.

Observed consequences: decoders that skip checksum verification accept
frames that other decoders reject.  In a dictionary-substitution
scenario (a decoder presented with a dictionary whose ID matches the
frame's Dictionary_ID but whose content differs), the substitution goes
undetected and silently corrupted output is produced wherever the
checksum is not verified; with verification performed, the corruption
is detected.

The correction removes the checksum from the class of ignorable fields
and asks for verification with SHOULD, matching its role as the
documented integrity mechanism (an "optional xxHash-64 checksum ...
for detection of data corruption", Section 3).  Note that this document
does not use RFC 2119 keywords; "SHOULD" in the corrected text is
proposed with its customary meaning.

errata.orig: Each repeat offset must have a value less than the dictionary size.
errata.correct: Each repeat offset must have a value less than or equal to the dictionary content size and cannot be 0.
errata.notes:
The bound refers to the whole dictionary, but only the Content is
usable as history: the following paragraph states that the content
acts as a past and is what sequence commands reference, so an offset
between the content size and the dictionary size can never be used.
The current bound also does not exclude an offset of 0, which is not
meaningful.  The reference format description states the constraint as
a value less than or equal to the dictionary content size that cannot
equal 0.  The correction adopts that wording; RFC 9659 does not affect
this section.

errata.orig:
Number_of_Sequences is a variable size field using between 1 and 3 bytes.  If the first byte is "byte0":

   *  if (byte0 == 0): there are no sequences.  The sequence section
      stops here.  Decompressed content is defined entirely as
      Literals_Section content.  The FSE tables used in Repeat_Mode are
      not updated.

   *  if (byte0 < 128): Number_of_Sequences = byte0.  Uses 1 byte.

   *  if (byte0 < 255): Number_of_Sequences = ((byte0 - 128) << 8) +
      byte1.  Uses 2 bytes.

   *  if (byte0 == 255): Number_of_Sequences = byte1 + (byte2 << 8) +
      0x7F00.  Uses 3 bytes.
errata.correct:
Number_of_Sequences is a variable size field using between 1 and 3 bytes.  If the first byte is "byte0":

   *  if (byte0 < 128): Number_of_Sequences = byte0.  Uses 1 byte.

   *  if (byte0 < 255): Number_of_Sequences = ((byte0 - 128) << 8) +
      byte1.  Uses 2 bytes.

   *  if (byte0 == 255): Number_of_Sequences = byte1 + (byte2 << 8) +
      0x7F00.  Uses 3 bytes.

   If Number_of_Sequences is 0, there are no sequences.  The sequence
   section stops here.  Decompressed content is defined entirely as
   Literals_Section content.  The FSE tables used in Repeat_Mode are
   not updated.
errata.notes:
The zero test is written against the first byte, but the 2-byte form
can also yield 0: byte0 = 128 and byte1 = 0 gives
((128 - 128) << 8) + 0 = 0.  For that encoding the "no sequences"
branch is not taken, so the text does not say whether
Symbol_Compression_Modes is read or whether the Repeat_Mode tables are
updated, which affects subsequent blocks.  The reference format
description tests the decoded value instead and notes that the 2-byte
form fully overlaps the 1-byte form.  The correction moves the zero
test after the three value branches and applies it to the decoded
value.  RFC 9659 updates the Window_Size limit in Section 3.1.1.1.2 and
does not affect this section.
